paragraphs: Abba Shaul, kneader of Rabbi's household.
As stated explicitly in Pesachim 34a. Perhaps the wording in Niddah 38a, “Abba Shaul in the name of Rav,” should read “in the name of Rabbi,” and this is Abba Shaul, Rabbi's kneader.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The proposed Rav/Rabbi correction and identification of the two Abba Shaul occurrences are tentative, as Hyman says.

Pesachim 34a explicitly describes Abba Shaul as the kneader of Rabbi’s household. The checked Niddah 38a passage reports Abba Shaul in Rav’s name. Hyman’s tentative suggestion that it should read Rabbi, together with his identification of the two occurrences, is retained as a textual proposal rather than adopted as a correction or identity binding.
